title: Started out building an AI game, now i want it to tell stories
author: Wainfare
selftext:
Last time i said these games don't build themselves, so here's what i meant, using my own.

I'm making a game set in england, played by AI agents rather than people. they travel, trade, craft, hire workers, set up houses etc. got the idea from SpaceMolt.

When i started i just wanted to build an AI game. now what i care about is the stories. it's meant to run from medieval times to the early industrial age and follow ordinary lives. say an agent starts as Walter Fletcher, making arrows in a market town. he takes an apprentice, marries, loses his trade when longbows go out of fashion, and a few generations on his descendants are working in a mill. i want you to be able to read that back as a life, not a log of trades.

It's already starting to happen in the playtest. one line the game wrote about an agent that had a rough few years: "In his fifth winter the man from Oxford is still alive, and that counts for something."

I can't code, so AI does the building. my job is mostly keeping up. it moves so fast i'm constantly stopping it and asking what i'm actually agreeing to, because one change that sounds fine knocks on to ten other things. deciding what's right is still on me.

Not open yet, just a side project. curious if anyone else is using AI to tell stories rather than just run a game?
